newsitem.title: UK: N.Sea wet market firm, but Brent paper weakens late.
newsitem.headline: N.Sea wet market firm, but Brent paper weakens late.

text.p: Differentials for North Sea crudes were firmer on Friday, supported by scarce early February supplies and prompt short-covering requirements.
While Brent intermonth spreads and CFDs eased back in late talk, there were no signs of weakness on the physical market.
The third of the day's Brent dates was kept ahead of the five o'clock deadline by a Wall Street trader, underscoring the wet market's strength.
The other two Brent cargoes nominated from the paper chains were kept early and quickly onsold at firm premiums.
A Feb 9-11 cargo was traded at Feb Brent +2 cents, and a Feb 10-13 loader was sold at March Brent +48 cents, up 20 cents on the last March-related deal.
"I find it impossible to believe that (this market) can go anywhere but down," said one trader.
But other North Sea grades were also commanding healthy differentials, with an mid-Feb Ekofisk heard traded at Dated Brent +27 cents and a Gulfaks C at Dated +55 cents.
The February Ekofisk loading programme, released on Friday, scheduled 14.1 million barrels of liftings for the month, a reduction of around 30,000 barrels per day on January.
On the paper market, Brent intermonth spreads eased back in late discussion. Feb/Mar was valued around +42/44 having traded earlier at +44 cents.
CFDs also weakened, with next week's dates talked at March Brent +31/+35, having traded at +35. The following week was valued at March Brent +23 cents.
March Brent was trading slightly down at $22.35/$22.40 a barrel at 1830 GMT in line with the IPE screen.
In the Mediterranean, the market for Urals was still seen firm, with differentials assessed in the (Dated Brent) -60s.
